sections.body: A fraction like 3/4 means 3 parts out of 4 equal parts. The bottom number (denominator) says how many parts the whole is cut into.
Same denominator? Just compare the tops. 5/8 is bigger than 3/8 because 5 pieces is more than 3 pieces of the same size.
Same numerator? The SMALLER denominator wins! 1/3 is bigger than 1/5, because a pizza cut into 3 has bigger slices than one cut into 5.
Different tops and bottoms? Make the denominators the same. For 2/3 and 3/4, use twelfths: 2/3 = 8/12 and 3/4 = 9/12. So 3/4 is bigger.
Fold two paper strips the same length. Fold one into 3 parts and one into 4. Shade 2/3 and 3/4 and compare.

hints: Look at the denominators. Are they the same?
With the same size pieces, more pieces means…?
Example: 3/7 vs 6/7 — same pieces (sevenths), and 6 pieces is more than 3.
quiz.explain: Both are fifths. 4 fifths is more than 2 fifths, so 4/5 is bigger.

hints: The tops are the same. Think about slice size.
A cake cut into more pieces gives smaller pieces.
Example: 1/2 vs 1/10 — half a pizza is much more than one tenth. Same idea here.
quiz.explain: Cutting into 4 gives bigger pieces than cutting into 6, so 1/4 is bigger.

hints: Try to make the denominators the same.
Both 6 and 4 go into 12. Turn both into twelfths.
Example: 1/2 vs 2/5 → tenths: 5/10 vs 4/10, so 1/2 is bigger. Now do 5/6 and 3/4 with twelfths.
quiz.explain: 5/6 = 10/12 and 3/4 = 9/12. 10/12 is bigger, so 5/6 is bigger.
